rv.q: Duchovny virtually never leaves the stage for 90 minutes and he tries hard to show that he's not just a TV and film actor. This latest revival of 'The Ritz' is cute, cuddly and often oddly inert.
But the plush production only serves to expose the play’s weaknesses.
Mantello’s production feels mechanical, without titillation, and we are rarely engaged in the heat of the pursuit.
Duchovny's deeply-felt performance is abetted by three fine actors depicting two characters each.

cn.t: McNally's 1975 gay bathhouse farce feels dated in revival despite energetic performances and Scott Pask's striking set design. The once-risqué comedy now plays as tame, though the cast commits fully to the physical humor.

vs.sum: An intimate 299-seat black box space at Roundabout, offering an unusually close actor-audience experience unlike any other Broadway house. Sightlines and sound vary by configuration since staging changes per production. Comfort is adequate but unremarkable.

acc.note: Accessible by elevator only. Assistive listening devices available.
